“Ba’zi odamlar universitetda o‘qish ishg: “Some people believe that a university education is not necessary to get a job.” To what extent do you agree with this opinion? Give reasons and examples.
“Bugun bandman.” → U o‘sha kuni band eka: “I'm busy today.” → She said she was busy that day.
“By” — o‘sha vaqtgacha tugagan: will hav: “By” — finished by that time: will have + V3.
Use the patterns “Due to ...” (cause) and “This leads to ...” (effect) or “could be done” (solution)
“Hadn’t it been” emas: Had it not been: Not “Hadn’t it been”: Had it not been
“I am boring” means “I am a boring person”.
“I am writing to inform you” — rasmiy us: “I am writing to inform you” — formal style.
“I see what you mean, but…” — an objection.
“I want…” — juda to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri, qo‘: “I want…” is very direct and can sound rude. In a café the polite form is: “I’d like a coffee, please.” (I’d = I would).
“Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar foydalimi?” mavzusid: Write an essay paragraph on “Is social media useful?”: with much as, adjective + as / though and be that as it may.
“Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar yoshlarga zarar yetk: “Do social networks harm young people?” — write 3 sentences in cautious language (may, tend to, it could be argued…).
“In my opinion / I believe that ...” qo‘: Add “In my opinion / I believe that ...”
“It is clear to me” — a personal opinion.
“Kitob” inglizchada qanday aytiladi?: How do you say “kitob” in English?
“ONE WORD ONLY” bitta so‘z degani. Ikkit: “ONE WORD ONLY” means one word. Two words is a wrong answer.
“Onlayn ta’lim an’anaviy darsdan yaxshim: “Is online learning better than traditional lessons?” — write 3–4 sentences giving both sides (although / however / despite).
“Onlayn ta’lim yoki an’anaviy ta’lim?” m: Write a paragraph on “Online learning or traditional learning?”: with whereas, given that and provided that / as long as.
“O‘zim, yolg‘iz” ma’nosida: by myself (I: In the meaning “alone, on my own”: by myself (I did it by myself). each other — “one another”: “They love each other.” (not themselves: “They love themselves” — each loves himself!)
“Qanday aytiladi” — How do you say…?: “How is it said” — How do you say…?
“Shahrimizga velosiped yo‘laklari kerak”: Write a short speech on “Our city needs cycle lanes”: with a rhetorical question, a triple and a contrasting pair.
“Shifting register” darsida phrasal verb: In the “Shifting register” lesson we learned to replace a phrasal verb with a formal verb (find out → ascertain). But not every phrasal verb is informal! Some are very widely used in academic papers: carry out research (conduct research), account for 40% (make up), rule out a possibility (exclude), bring about change (cause), point out (note).
“Talabalar ishlashi kerakmi?” mavzusida: Write a balanced paragraph on “Should students work?”: with opinion, counter-argument and conclusion phrases.
“Texnologiya jamiyatni yaxshilaydimi?” m: Write 4–5 sentences on “Does technology improve society?”: generalising without articles and the + adjective (the young, the elderly).
“The visit was ___ friendly, but there w: “The visit was ___ friendly, but there was tension.” (on the face of it)
“The … of” — a noun is needed: construction.
“There is / There are” yoki “has” ishlat: “There is / There are” or “has” is used
“True” matnda aytilgan degani, ehtimoli: “True” means the text says it, not that it is likely.
“We've finished.” → They said they had finished.
“Tug‘ilmoq” — was/were born: “I was born: “To be born” — was/were born: “I was born on 12th June.” “He was born in 2001.” on with a day, in with a month or year.
“Turning now to” — yangi bo‘lim: economi: “Turning now to” — a new section: economic effects.
“What time does…?” yoki “How long does…?: there is a question “What time does…?” or “How long does…?”
“Where are you from?” yoki “What do you: “Where are you from?” or “What do you do?” is used
“Would you like…?” — taklif. “Do you lik: “Would you like…?” is an offer. “Do you like…?” asks whether you like something in general. Would you like a tea? ≠ Do you like tea?
“by” (… gacha) va “by the time” ko‘pinch: “by” (up to) and “by the time” often go with the future perfect.
“explain why” — the place to speak in more depth.
“failed” — birinchisi haqida (distractor: “failed” is about the first one (a distractor).
“local” bo‘lsa ham, tug‘ilgan joyi aytil: Even though it says “local”, the place of birth isn't stated → NOT GIVEN.
“neither … nor” da fe’l yaqin turgan ega: With “neither … nor”, the verb agrees with the nearer subject: the teacher → was.
“outweigh” / “on balance” bilan qaysi to: Say which side weighs more with “outweigh” / “on balance”
“reopened in July” — to‘g‘ri, lekin savo: “reopened in July” — true, but not the answer to the question.
“result to / lead in” emas: result in /: Not “result to / lead in”: result in / lead to
“very” o‘rniga sifatning tabiiy juftini: Instead of “very”, you’ll pick the adjective’s natural partner (highly, deeply, widely, bitterly, fully, entirely) and express your ideas more precisely in Speaking and Writing.
“yo‘q” ma’nosida mustn’t have emas: can’: In the meaning “no”, not mustn’t have: can’t have
